site.title: Engawa Works

categories.name: Neighbourhood

posts.title: A week of Thursday dinners
posts.excerpt: What happens to the long kitchen table between six and ten on a Thursday, and who does the washing up.
posts.content:
At six the last laptops close. By half past, the long table in the kitchen has a rice cooker at one end and whatever people brought at the other.

There is no programme. Someone introduces the newest member; someone else asks who has a spare monitor cable. The washing up is done by whoever arrived last.

posts.title: Raking the courtyard
posts.excerpt: Every Monday morning the gravel round the pine is raked into new rings, and the veranda fills up a little earlier each day.
posts.content:
The pine in the courtyard is older than the house. Every Monday at eight the host rakes the gravel around it into new rings; it takes twenty minutes and nobody is allowed to help.

On the veranda, people start bringing blankets. The low tables stay out until the first frost.

posts.title: How the quiet room stays quiet
posts.excerpt: Three small rules, a felt door seal and a clock with no tick: what keeps the upstairs room silent.
posts.content:
No calls, no music, keyboards at a whisper. The rules fit on a card by the door and they have not changed since the first week.

The rest is the building: a felt seal on the sliding door, plaster walls, and a wall clock chosen because it does not tick.

posts.title: Notes from the board by the door
posts.excerpt: Lost umbrellas, a bicycle for sale, a reading group: a month of the bulletin board.
posts.content:
The board by the door is where the house talks to itself. This month: two umbrellas waiting for owners, a reading group on Tuesdays, a spare bicycle.

Pin what you like. The hosts clear it on the first of the month and keep anything that still matters.

posts.title: Oiling the cedar boards
posts.excerpt: Twice a year the veranda gets a coat of oil, and members trade an hour of work for tea by the pine.
posts.content:
Cedar weathers grey if you let it. Twice a year, on a Saturday morning, we oil the veranda boards by hand, one row at a time.

It takes about an hour with eight people. Afterwards there is tea, and the boards smell of the forest for a week.

posts.title: A walk round Nishioka at lunch
posts.excerpt: Tofu at the corner, the bicycle repairer, the shrine steps: a twenty-minute loop for a lunch break.
posts.content:
Turn left out of the door. The tofu shop sells out by one; the bicycle repairer will look at your brakes while you wait.

Up the shrine steps, along the canal, and you are back in twenty minutes with something warm for the long table.
